_comment: Cornerman lobby jokes (Kyle, 2026-08-25). Played ONLY in the pre-fight lobby — never inside a round, never on the rhythm map. Rendered conversational: work performance, land finish, no tempo fit.

jokes.text: My cornerman told me to stick and move. So I glued myself to the canvas, and changed gyms.
Between rounds, my cornerman whispered, you've got him right where you want him. I said, standing up?
I asked my cornerman for a winning strategy. He handed me a bus schedule out of town.
My cornerman is brutally honest. After round three, he said, good news, the swelling is hiding your bruises.
I told my cornerman I couldn't see out of my left eye. He said, perfect. Now you won't see half the punches coming.
My cornerman said I needed to throw more combinations. Apparently, jab, cross, apologize, doesn't count.
The referee asked whether I wanted to continue. My cornerman answered, he didn't want to start.
My cornerman is also my therapist. Between rounds, he asks, and how did that uppercut make you feel?
I complained that my opponent kept hitting me below the belt. My cornerman said, at least he respects your face.
After I got knocked down, my cornerman yelled, take the eight count! I said, can I take the rest of the week?
I started boxing to get in shape. Now the shape I'm in is, slightly dented.
My boxing coach told me to work on my footwork. So I learned how to run away much more gracefully.
Boxing is a lot like chess. Except every time you make a bad move, the other player punches you.
I tried shadowboxing, but my shadow won by split decision.
My opponent had an unbeatable record. Fortunately, I was able to add one more win to it.
The referee told us to protect ourselves at all times. So I immediately called my insurance company.
I'm not saying my defense is bad, but my face has blocked every punch so far.
My coach said I have a glass jaw. I prefer to think of it as premium crystal.
I entered the ring feeling like a million bucks. I left looking like loose change.
I asked the boxer why he kept a pencil in his glove. He said he wanted to draw a knockout.
My heavy bag has seen me at my strongest, my weakest, and whatever that thing was on cardio day.
I hit the heavy bag for stress relief. The bag is now the one who needs therapy.
My heavy bag doesn't hit back. That's why it's still my favorite sparring partner.
The heavy bag and I have an understanding. I punch it, and it silently judges my technique.
I spent thirty minutes beating up the heavy bag. It still looked better than I did afterward.
I told my heavy bag I was taking a rest day. I swear I saw it relax.
My heavy bag swings harder after I miss it, than I ever do on purpose.
The only thing I've knocked out at the gym, is my heavy bag's warranty.
My heavy bag has absorbed so many bad punches, it deserves hazard pay.
Every time I think I'm getting good, the heavy bag reminds me it's literally standing still.
